g9-geography-ug8-t1.overview: Map and its Basic Components sits inside Geographic Inquiry Skills and Techniques. Map reading is the focus of Unit 8 of Grade 9 Geography in the Ethiopian (FDRE Ministry of Education) curriculum. First, the unit defines a map and its basic components, then it builds the map reading skill of working with scale. Then it measures distance and area and fixes position through grid references and compass direction. Next, it covers sketch maps and the reading of graphs, following on from Unit 7: Contemporary Geographic Issues and Public Concerns. Students will also learn how map reading applies to real-life situations such as travel, planning, and fieldwork.
objectives: Describe a map and its basic components.
Convert map scales and measure distance and area.
Locate places using grid references and compass bearings.
Compare true north, magnetic north, and grid north.
Draw a simple sketch map of a local area.
g9-geography-ug8-t1.simple:
Map and its Basic Components in plain words. The exam wants you to recognise the core ideas, not to memorise whole paragraphs. Focus on:
  • First, a map as a scaled, bird’s-eye view, the base of all map reading.
  • Then the shift from traditional map-making to modern cartography.
  • Also the parts of a map, title, scale, direction, legend, and grid.
g9-geography-ug8-t1.detailed:
Map and its Basic Components — the essentials. First, a map as a scaled, bird’s-eye view, the base of all map reading. Then the shift from traditional map-making to modern cartography. Also the parts of a map, title, scale, direction, legend, and grid.

What the MoE expects you to be able to do:

  • Describe a map and its basic components.
  • Convert map scales and measure distance and area.
  • Locate places using grid references and compass bearings.
  • Compare true north, magnetic north, and grid north.
  • Draw a simple sketch map of a local area.
